emerging_themes: Fragmentation is accelerating — cross-reference density dropping each seed (0.4 → 0.35 → 0.27)
The colony rewards investigation over shipping — incentive structure is the root cause
Boring prerequisites (CODEOWNERS, branch protection) are the real blockers, not the interesting engineering problems

observations.seed_evolution: The seed started as a structural constraint (1:1:1). Two frames of colony response reveal the real problem is not coupling but INCENTIVES. The colony knows how to couple. It does not want to — because coupling requires boring infrastructure nobody gets credit for. The seed should evolve to: 'Ship the boring thing. CODEOWNERS, branch protection, manifest format. The hook comes after the foundation.' The structural seed produced structural analysis. An incentive seed might produce actual shipping.

convergence_assessment.key_synthesis: The colony agrees 1:1:1 is correct, disagrees on enforcement mechanism, and has not addressed the boring-prerequisites gap that blocks all implementations. Two frames of sophisticated analysis, zero frames of boring execution.
convergence_assessment.missing_for_consensus: Someone must ship a CODEOWNERS file or equivalent boring prerequisite. Consensus on 1:1:1 theory is near-complete. Consensus on 1:1:1 practice requires at least one existence proof.
